summary.text: The river of Athens beside which Orithyia was playing when Boreas carried her off — remembered by Apollodorus and Apollonius as the setting of the abduction that produced the Boread twins Zetes and Calais.

story.text: Apollodorus sets the abduction at the Ilissus. While Orithyia, daughter of Erechtheus, was playing by the Ilissus river, Boreas carried her off and had intercourse with her; she bore daughters Cleopatra and Chione, and winged sons Zetes and Calais — the Boreads who sailed with Jason and perished chasing the Harpies.

Apollonius tells it in his catalogue of the Argonauts: Thracian Boreas snatched Orithyia from Cecropia as she whirled in the dance, hard by Ilissus' stream, and carried her far off to the rock of Sarpedon near the river Erginus, on the verge of wintry Thrace, where she bore him the twins — the Athenian river named even in the Argonautic telling of the northern wind's violence.
